author: Jun Lucis
programme_question: Can a history-conditioned boundary response structure remain measurably related across branch/topology reconfiguration even when state, geometry, and absolute response change?
non_claim_bearing_philosophical_motivati: Individuality as boundary-conditioned response lineage rather than unchanged content.

admissible_model_class.phi: dphi/dt = div(D(phi) grad(phi) + gamma |grad(phi)|^2 grad(phi)) - mu_eff(m) phi + S_base(x;q) + S_read(x,t;a)*(1+eta_S*m)
admissible_model_class.probe_window: beta_read=0; probe may not write new history; retained m may undergo frozen decay/diffusion
admissible_model_class.exact_coefficients: selected in B27-P0 for executability only, then frozen before B27.1

response_operator.estimator: symmetric finite differences at frozen h and h/2

response_pullback.primary_reason: remove one global response-gain degree of freedom and output-coordinate dependence

B27_3.purpose: prospective held-out transfer to a new reconfiguration family

forbidden: using P0 as positive claim evidence
choosing thresholds from claim-target effect sizes
promoting pilot cases to held-out evidence

anti_rescue: no new coupling term after first B27.1 claim trajectory
no domain extension solely to acquire desired reconfiguration
stop_rules: If B27.1 validly finds no history conditioning, no history-lineage claim may be made from later stages.
If B27.2 validly fails, A may not be tuned on that failed family inside B27.2.
B27.3 ends after the frozen held-out family regardless of outcome.
No B27 result changes B19-B26 verdicts.
source_alignment_note: Before any B27-P0 or claim-bearing trajectory, the admissible model class was aligned explicitly to the published B16 history-feedback equations; no B27 numerical outcome existed.
